learningObjectives: Contrast dorsal and ventral language pathways.
Identify major cortical contributors to comprehension and production.
Distinguish aphasia from dysarthria and apraxia of speech.
Use network-based rather than two-centre language models.

anatomy.label: Superior temporal cortex
anatomy.short: Analyse speech sounds and lexical patterns
anatomy.detail: Temporal auditory regions transform acoustic input into phonological representations.
anatomy.clinical: Damage can impair speech discrimination and comprehension.

anatomy.label: Ventral language stream
anatomy.short: Map sound and print to meaning
anatomy.detail: Middle and anterior temporal pathways integrate lexical-semantic information.
anatomy.clinical: Disruption may impair comprehension and semantic access.

anatomy.label: Dorsal language stream
anatomy.detail: Parietal and frontal pathways support repetition, phonological working memory and sensorimotor mapping.
anatomy.clinical: Damage can produce disproportionate repetition and phonological errors.

anatomy.label: Inferior frontal cortex
anatomy.detail: Left inferior frontal systems support controlled retrieval, syntax and speech planning.
anatomy.clinical: Lesions may reduce fluency and grammatical complexity.

anatomy.label: Right-hemisphere language systems
anatomy.detail: Right temporal and frontal regions contribute emotional tone and context-sensitive interpretation.
anatomy.clinical: Damage may impair humour, indirect meaning or emotional prosody.

interaction.title: Explore the Language Networks
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence.

stages.label: Analyse
stages.text: Auditory or visual systems extract speech sounds or written forms.

stages.label: Access
stages.text: Temporal networks activate candidate words and meanings.

stages.label: Sequence
stages.text: Frontal and dorsal pathways organise phonology, grammar and motor plans.

stages.label: Express
stages.text: Motor systems produce speech, writing or gesture while feedback updates performance.

quizBank.question: The dorsal language pathway is especially involved in:
quizBank.explanation: Dorsal frontotemporal pathways support phonological sensorimotor mapping and repetition.

quizBank.question: Ventral language pathways primarily support:
quizBank.explanation: Ventral temporal pathways are central to lexical-semantic processing.

quizBank.question: Aphasia is best defined as:
options: An acquired language disorder from brain dysfunction
Weakness of the speech muscles only
quizBank.explanation: Aphasia affects language formulation or comprehension and is distinct from pure motor-speech impairment.

quizBank.question: The right hemisphere commonly contributes to:
quizBank.explanation: Right-lateralised systems contribute emotional tone, pragmatic interpretation and discourse coherence.

quizBank.question: Modern language neuroscience favours:
quizBank.explanation: Language depends on distributed dorsal and ventral pathways with variable lateralisation.

prompts: Name the major components of the Language Networks.
Explain one clinically relevant function of the Language Networks.
Identify one common oversimplification to avoid.
